claims.quote: Because characteristic bone lesions occur only with relatively advanced disease, bone radiographs are recommended only for symptomatic patients. radiographs typically show bone cysts, a heterogeneous appearance of the skull, and subperiosteal resorption of bone in the phalanges and distal clavicles.

claims.text: In osteitis fibrosa cystica (often due to primary hyperparathyroidism), increased osteoclastic activity from PTH overstimulation causes rarefaction of bone with fibrous degeneration and cyst and fibrous nodule formation
claims.quote: In osteitis fibrosa cystica (often due to primary hyperparathyroidism), increased osteoclastic activity from overstimulation by PTH causes rarefaction of bone with fibrous degeneration and cyst and fibrous nodule formation.

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Labs: serum calcium is rarely > 12 mg/dL, but ionized serum calcium is almost always elevated; low serum phosphate suggests hyperparathyroidism, especially with elevated renal phosphate excretion; alkaline phosphatase is frequently increased when there is increased bone turnover; an increased intact PTH with an inappropriately high or high-normal serum calcium is diagnostic
claims.quote: In hyperparathyroidism, the serum calcium is rarely > 12 mg/dL (> 3 mmol/L), but the ionized serum calcium is almost always elevated. Low serum phosphate concentration suggests hyperparathyroidism, especially when coupled with elevated renal excretion of phosphate. When hyperparathyroidism results in increased bone turnover, serum alkaline phosphatase is frequently increased. An increased intact PTH with an inappropriately high or high-normal serum calcium level is diagnostic.

claims.text: Causes Primary hyperparathyroidism: excessive PTH secretion by one or more parathyroid glands; probably the most common cause of hypercalcemia, particularly in patients who are not hospitalized; incidence increases with age and is higher in postmenopausal women; also occurs in high frequency ≥ 3 decades after neck irradiation; familial and sporadic forms exist
claims.quote: Primary hyperparathyroidism is a generalized disorder resulting from excessive secretion of parathyroid hormone (PTH) by one or more parathyroid glands. It probably is the most common cause of hypercalcemia, particularly among patients who are not hospitalized. Incidence increases with age and is higher in postmenopausal women. It also occurs in high frequency ≥ 3 decades after neck irradiation. Familial and sporadic forms exist.

claims.text: Parathyroid adenoma in approximately 85% (sometimes difficult to distinguish from a normal gland), hyperplasia of ≥ 2 glands in approximately 15%, parathyroid cancer in < 1%
claims.quote: Histologic examination shows a parathyroid adenoma in approximately 85% of patients with primary hyperparathyroidism, although it is sometimes difficult to distinguish an adenoma from a normal gland. Approximately 15% of cases are due to hyperplasia of ≥ 2 glands. Parathyroid cancer occurs in < 1% of cases.

claims.text: Primary hyperparathyroidism causes hypophosphatemia and excessive bone resorption
claims.quote: Primary hyperparathyroidism causes hypophosphatemia and excessive bone resorption.

claims.text: Symptoms Hypercalcemia: in mild hypercalcemia many patients are asymptomatic; manifestations include constipation, anorexia, nausea and vomiting, abdominal pain, and ileus; polyuria, nocturia, and polydipsia; calcium > 12 mg/dL can cause emotional lability, confusion, delirium, psychosis, stupor, and coma; may cause neuromuscular symptoms, including skeletal muscle weakness; hypercalciuria with nephrolithiasis is common
claims.quote: In mild hypercalcemia, many patients are asymptomatic. Clinical manifestations of hypercalcemia include constipation, anorexia, nausea and vomiting, abdominal pain, and ileus. Impairment of the renal concentrating mechanism leads to polyuria, nocturia, and polydipsia. Elevation of serum calcium > 12 mg/dL (> 3.00 mmol/L) can cause emotional lability, confusion, delirium, psychosis, stupor, and coma. Hypercalcemia may cause neuromuscular symptoms, including skeletal muscle weakness. Hypercalciuria with nephrolithiasis is common.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Symptomatic or progressive hyperparathyroidism: surgery is indicated; indications for surgery in asymptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism are controversial
claims.quote: In patients with symptomatic or progressive hyperparathyroidism, surgery is indicated. The indications for surgery in patients with asymptomatic, primary hyperparathyroidism are controversial.

claims.text: Asymptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism with no indications for surgery may be treated conservatively: stay active, low-calcium diet, plenty of fluids, avoid medications that can raise serum calcium (eg, thiazide diuretics); serum calcium and renal function every 6 months, bone density every 12 months; subclinical bone disease, hypertension, and longevity are concerns; osteoporosis is treated with bisphosphonates
claims.quote: Patients with asymptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism with no indications for surgery may be treated conservatively with methods to ensure that serum calcium concentrations remain low. Patients should remain active (ie, avoid immobilization that could exacerbate hypercalcemia), follow a low-calcium diet, drink plenty of fluids to minimize the chance of nephrolithiasis, and avoid medications that can raise serum calcium, such as thiazide diuretics. Serum calcium level and renal function are monitored every 6 months. Bone density is monitored every 12 months. However, subclinical bone disease, hypertension, and longevity are concerns. Osteoporosis is treated with bisphosphonates.

claims.text: Severe hypercalcemia with primary hyperparathyroidism in patients unable to undergo parathyroidectomy: medical treatment is indicated; cinacalcet (a calcimimetic) may lower parathyroid hormone and calcium levels
claims.quote: In patients with severe hypercalcemia with primary hyperparathyroidism who are unable to undergo parathyroidectomy, medical treatment is indicated. Cinacalcet, a calcimimetic agent that increases the sensitivity of the calcium-sensing receptor to extracellular calcium, may lower parathyroid hormone and calcium levels.

claims.text: Secondary hyperparathyroidism: dietary phosphate restriction, phosphate binders (eg, calcium carbonate, sevelamer); on dialysis, consider cautious vitamin D analogs or cinacalcet, or parathyroidectomy
claims.quote: Treat patients with secondary hyperparathyroidism with dietary phosphate restriction, phosphate binders such as calcium carbonate or sevelamer; in those on dialysis, consider cautious administration of vitamin D analogs or cinacalcet, or parathyroidectomy.
